slides.title: Acquisition and display are separate clocks
slides.lead: A 50 Hz sensor does not require 50 complete screen redraws/s.
points: Lab 9.3 meter: nominal 10 Hz
Lab 9.4 chart input: 50 samples/s, five columns per update by default
Lab 9.4 bubble: nominal 10 Hz
Actual rates depend on host and link load
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Sweep across the chart
slides.lead: Write new columns and wrap the cursor to the left.
points: Old columns stay until the cursor reaches them
Scrolling shifts the whole history; sweeping does not
A sweep boundary joins different time intervals: read the cursor
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Create a three-trace StripChart
slides.lead: Each channel has its own range and colour.
points: ranges=[(-20,20)]*3 creates three identical ranges
x=4,y=50,w=312,h=90 places the chart in the body
px_per_sample defaults to 1; cols_per_update defaults to 5
slides.code:
chart = rk.StripChart(d, ranges=[(-20, 20)] * 3,
    colors=[rk.Color.RED, rk.Color.GREEN, rk.Color.BLUE],
    x=4, y=50, w=312, h=90)
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Turn a value into a screen y
slides.lead: High values map upward, although screen y grows downward.
points: fraction=(value−lo)/(hi−lo), clipped to [0,1]
y = top + round((1−fraction)·(height−1))
Out-of-range samples flatten at the edge; clipping can hide amplitude
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: How long does 312 pixels remember?
points: Two pixels/sample show 3.12 s at the same width
More visual detail means less time history
Change pixels/sample and observe the cursor wrap sooner
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Circular state avoids moving everything
slides.lead: A write index wraps modulo the display width.
points: The browser keeps a fixed buffer of recent columns
The SDK queues only new chart columns and remembers each trace’s last y
This is a design pattern; the SDK implementation is not a general ring-buffer class
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Flush only when drawing was queued
slides.lead: push returns a count of newly queued columns.
points: Zero means the batching threshold has not been reached
The bubble may still queue operations on every fifth sample
The lab flushes when either source has something to draw
slides.code:
drawn = chart.push(s.ax, s.ay, s.az)
# ... bubble update may set drawn ...
if drawn:
    d.flush()
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: A bubble is a tilt cue
slides.lead: At rest, acceleration components indicate gravity direction.
points: Lab mapping: ax/g and ay/g, independently clipped
reach=LEVEL_R−BUBBLE_R=27 pixels
A physically plausible static vector stays inside the circle
Dynamic acceleration can move the cue outside the dial: this is not a full orientation estimator
slides.notes: The agreed sketch suggested radial limiting; the actual lab clips axes independently. The demonstration offers both with labels rather than silently changing the lab behavior.

slides.title: Erase the old bubble, then repair the dial
slides.lead: A moving object needs a remembered previous position.
points: Erase old circle in dial colour; draw new circle yellow
Redraw crosshairs because the bubble can cover them
Skip drawing when integer coordinates did not change
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.

slides.title: Run the chart and level together
slides.lead: Tilt slowly first; then shake and explain the difference.
points: Slow tilt makes a useful level cue
Shake mixes dynamic acceleration with gravity
Record chart.dropped and link stats; distinguish display drops from IMU losses
slides.notes: Have students predict why the level is unreliable during shaking. Do not label all movement as orientation change.

slides.title: Measure the system, not just the animation
slides.lead: A smooth browser canvas is not a device performance measurement.
points: Count successful display updates over elapsed time
d.stats counts link commands; updates can use several commands
ImuStream.lost concerns acquisition; chart.dropped concerns chart backlog
Report hardware, firmware, source mode and duration with a measurement
slides.notes: Ask students to predict the result before revealing or running it. Connect the observation to the lab source linked on this slide.
